notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix. §1985:VI.5.9.3 SR3 has two sentences. The first ("The lowercase letters corresponding to the uppercase letters representing the PICTURE symbols A, B, P, S, V, X, Z, CR, and DB are equivalent to their uppercase representations") is implemented: TryExpandRepeats folds the whole character-string with ToUpperInvariant before any symbol is read, so pic aaa, 9ppp, s9v9, zz9, xbx, 99db and 99Cr bind as their uppercase forms at 85 (probed; the witness runs x, s, v, z, cr and b). The second ("All other lowercase letters are not equivalent to their corresponding uppercase representations") is not: the same blanket fold, and the char.ToUpperInvariant in AnalyzeCharacterString's scan for the currency symbol, apply at every edition with no 1985 arm, so a lowercase letter is taken as the uppercase letter the CURRENCY SIGN clause names. §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR11 lets the currency symbol be an uppercase letter other than A, B, C, D, P, R, S, V, X, Z and never a lowercase one ("the lowercase letters a through z" are excepted), so under CURRENCY SIGN IS "W" the character w is no PICTURE symbol at all and PIC w99 is not an allowable combination (§1985:VI.5.9.3 SR2). At --std 85 it compiles and edits as PIC W99. The fold is the 2023 rule (kb/Work PB534, landed, measured the lowercase currency letter binding and judged it by the 2023 text only).

next.reason: 1985 makes only the lowercase forms of A, B, P, S, V, X, Z, CR and DB equivalent, and 'All other lowercase letters are not equivalent', which includes a letter chosen as the currency symbol. §2023:13.18.40.3 SR3 refers symbols other than the currency symbol to §2023:8.1.3.2 GR3, under which basic letters outside literals are 'treated in a case-insensitive manner'. It refers currency symbols to §2023:12.3.7.3 SR20, whose NOTE 2 says 'N'M', N'm', 'M', and 'm' used as currency symbols are all equivalent'. A lowercase occurrence of a letter currency symbol, not equivalent in 1985, is equivalent in 2023.
